about: Voice memos the author recorded while listening to a narrated draft of the book, each transcribed and pinned to the word that was playing when the recording started (pins can be off by a few words). Work from `memos`: every entry carries its transcript plus the manuscript text it refers to (`location.sentence`, `location.paragraph`) and where that text is (`location.heading_path`), so the full manuscript doesn't need to be read; open the source only around a memo's location. `location.source` gives line/column/offset in the rendered markdown (`book.source_file`). When editing a different source format (e.g. the LaTeX the markdown was rendered from), use `heading_path` to find the file and search for `location.anchor_phrase`, allowing for differences in quotes, dashes, emphasis and footnote markup. `transcript_quality` is "no_speech" when the memo seems to be silence (whisper then tends to output filler like "you"). The pin is the word playing about a second before the button press, to allow for the press itself; when that lands in a different sentence from the press, `location.press_sentence` gives the sentence playing at the press, and the memo may be about either. `location.preceding` holds the sentences heard just before the pinned one, for memos that refer back ("a few seconds back", "that last sentence"). `continues_memo` marks a memo that carries on the previous one's thought. `listening` says what was actually heard: don't read the absence of memos on a section as approval unless it was heard.
